Pursuant to the Governor's Executive Order N-29-20, Planning Commission Members will be participating via
teleconference.

- Commission meeting videos are live-streamed on the City’s website at www.rhe.city/agendas and available for
viewing thereafter. Commission meetings are recorded for minutes preparation purposes.

- Members of the public may listen to the meeting live by calling: (1-669-900-6833) from any phone, Meeting ID:
857 0852 7044 Passcode: 941354. (Please note you will not have the ability to speak using the call-in option from
a phone line.)

-  Public  correspondence  may  be  emailed  to  Carol Corea, Administrative  Assistant  at
carolc@rollinghillsestatesca.gov. Emails received before 5:00 p.m. the night of the meeting will be forwarded to
the Commission for their consideration and included as part of the record.

- Members of the public may comment online using eComment on the “Meeting Agendas, Minutes & Videos”
page of the City’s website (www.rhe.city/agendas). Once the agenda is published, there will be an “eComment”
button next to the linked agenda under "Upcoming Events". Follow this link to the City’s SpeakUp page. After
you register, you may comment on any item on that particular agenda. These comments can be seen by the
public, will be considered by the Commission and become part of the record.

- Members of the public who wish to speak during this meeting, may join by visiting http://www.zoom.com/join
and enter the following credentials: Meeting ID: 857 0852 7044 Passcode: 941354.

- If using a tablet or phone, download the Zoom app and enter the following credentials: Meeting ID: 857 0852
7044 Passcode: 941354.

Members of the public who join the Zoom meeting will not have video, and may request to speak using the
following process: After joining the Zoom meeting, if you wish to speak, please select the "raise hand" option at
the lower portion of your screen. The host will send you a chat message to identify which item on the agenda you
would like to speak on and will unmute your mic at the appropriate time.

Agenda reports and other disclosable public records relating to each agenda item are available on the City's
website under Meeting Agendas, Minutes & Videos at www.rhe.city/agendas.

MINUTES
  PLANNING COMMISSION MEETING
  MONDAY, APRIL 5, 2021

  A regular meeting of the Planning Commission of the City of Rolling Hills Estates was called to
  order by CHAIR EDLER at 7:00 p.m. Pursuant to the Governor’s Executive Order N-29-20, this
  meeting was held via teleconference.

  2.  SALUTE TO THE FLAG

  CHAIR EDLER led those assembled in the Pledge of Allegiance.

  3.  ROLL CALL

  Commissioner’s Present:  Edler, Scott, Carman, Medawar, Schachter, Yoo, Zigrang

  Staff Member’s Present:  David Wahba, Director of Community Development and Public
  Works
  Jeannie Naughton, Planning Manager
  Carol Corea, Administrative Assistant

  4.  APPROVAL OF MINUTES

  A.  APPROVAL OF PLANNING COMMISSION MINUTES, MARCH 1, 2021.

  VICE CHAIR SCOTT made a motion, seconded by COMMISSIONER CARMAN to,

  APPROVE THE PLANNING COMMISSION MEETING MINUTES OF MARCH 1, 2021.

  There being no objection, CHAIR EDLER so ordered.

  5.  AUDIENCE ITEMS

  NONE

  6.  CONSENT CALENDAR

  A.  Reading in full of all ordinances and resolutions presented for consideration to the Planning
  Commission will be waived and all such ordinances and resolutions will be read by title only.

  COMMISSIONER SCHACHTER moved, seconded by COMMISSIONER CARMAN to,

  APPROVE ITEM 6A

  There being no objection, CHAIR EDLER so ordered.

  7.  BUSINESS ITEMS

  A.  PLANNING APPLICATION NO. PA-210076; ADDRESS: 2715 PALOS VERDES DRIVE
  NORTH; APPLICANT: DAVID AND HELEN SHAW; A request for a Grading Application (G-
  210077) for unpermitted grading, replacement of the existing driveway and driveway apron
  within the City's right-of-way, enlargement of the existing horse corrals, creation of orchard
  areas, and addition of decomposed granite trails around the property.

  Planning Manager Naughton provided a presentation summarizing the staff report for Planning
  Application No. PA-210076.

  Planning Manager Naughton stated that staff recommends that the Planning Commission approve
  Planning Application No. 210076 to approve a Grading Permit (GR-210077) subject to the
  conditions of approval described in the staff report.

  COMMISSIONER ZIGRANG stated that he will be living within a 500’ radius and stated that he
  knows the applicant and stated that he can look at this application without any reservations of
  conflicts.

  David Shaw, Applicant, stated that he would like to remove the straight asphalt driveway and make
  it nicer and improve the area between the house and the barn. In addition, he would like to move
  the dirt from one location to another and create a walkway around the house and add more fruit
  trees.

PLANNING COMMISSION MEETING
MINUTES, APRIL 5, 2021
  1
   VICE CHAIR SCOTT made a motion, seconded by COMMISSIONER CARMAN to,

  APPROVE PLANNING APPLICATION NO. 210076 AS PRESENTED.

  AYES: Edler, Scott, Carman, Medawar, Schachter, Yoo, Zigrang
  NOES:
  ABSENT:
  ABSTAIN:

  Planning Manager Naughton stated that the Planning Commission has approved Planning
  Application No. 210076, and there will be a 20-day appeal period where any member of the public
  may appeal this decision to the City Council.

  B.  ROOFING MATERIALS - METAL STANDING SEAM

  Planning Manager Naughton stated staff has received requests to allow metal standing seam roofs
  on the primary residence. Over the last several years, they have been allowed on out-buildings
  and as an accent material. Staff has received positive feedback from the community on metal
  standing seam roofs on the homes at The Residences at Rolling Hills Country Club. Staff brought
  this item to the City Council at their Policy Development Session in March and the City Council was
  supportive of allowing metal standing seam as a primary roofing material when appropriate. Staff
  was directed to report to the Planning Commission a supportive policy provision in allowing
  standing seam metal as the primary roofing material when appropriate.

  Planning Manager Naughton stated that staff is requesting direction from the Planning Commission
  on whether or not there is support at the commission level to allow standing seam metal as a
  roofing material. If so, it can be added to the city’s allowable roofing material handout. If the
  Planning Commission would prefer that staff develop a very specific criteria when metal standing
  seam is allowed, staff will bring it back to the planning commission to review.

  Planning Manager Naughton stated that staff would recommend not to allow bright reds, greens
  but rather the darker grays and earth tones.

  VICE CHAIR SCOTT asked what restrictions staff would place on metal standing seam roofs.

  Director Wahba stated that it would need to be a professional quality installation. Some of the
  criteria would include the width between the standing seams, detail on installation, and matte finish.
  The colors allowed should be a charcoal gray or browns and prohibit greens, blues, reds or white.
  In addition, ridges, end cap details and rain gutter systems should be addressed. This material
  could work with any architectural styles, with the exception of Spanish or Mediterranean. Staff
  would need to work with the property owners and homeowners associations that have specific
  CC&Rs.

  In response to a question from COMMISSIONER SCHACHTER, Director Wahba stated that
  applications will not be brought to the commission for Neighborhood Compatibility since they are
  currently not allowed. A proposed metal standing seam roof may be seen in applications for major
  remodels or new construction, which will be brought to the Planning Commission for review.
  Planning Manager Naughton added that anytime a better level of objective criteria is provided to
  applicants, there is less uncertainty in staff’s total discretion to approve or not approve an
  application.

  COMMISSIONER YOO asked what the major drawback is for allowing metal standing seam.
  COMMISSIONER ZIGRANG stated that this roofing material is very good, durable and does not
  rust.

  COMMISSIONER CARMAN commented that she fully supports having written guidelines. This
  roofing material can make a home look modern. COMMISSIONER CARMAN also asked for
  clarification on the Plantation style referenced in the staff report. Director Wahba stated that there
  are Plantation style homes in the city, which is not the typical Hawaiian influence, but share some
  of the features seen with Ranch style homes. Director Wahba agreed that the metal standing seam
  roof tends to give a home a modern application. COMMISSIONER CARMAN expressed her
  concern with allowing this type of roofing material.

  COMMISSIONER ZIGRANG stated that metal standing seam roofs have been around for
  hundreds of years. They are not for every house and the minimum roof pitch should be 3:12.

  COMMISSIONER MEDAWAR asked if they can be allowed for new construction only. Director
  Wahba stated that it can be, but it would be difficult to deny a similar home that is proposing this

PLANNING COMMISSION MEETING
MINUTES, APRIL 5, 2021
  2
   roofing material. Applications should be reviewed on a case-by-case basis.

  COMMISSIONER MEDAWAR stated that the concerns would be quality of installation and color.

  VICE CHAIR SCOTT stated that he is supportive of most of what has been discussed, however
  commented that he would not restrict to only dark colors.

  The Planning Commission directed staff to develop guidelines to be reviewed at a future Planning
  Commission meeting.

  8.  PUBLIC HEARINGS

  NONE

  9.  COMMISSION ITEMS

  COMMISSIONER SCHACHTER asked about the hours of operation for Rolling Hills Country Club.
  Director Wahba stated that there is nothing specific in the CUP regarding hours to mow the lawn; it
  is typical of a golf course to do grooming in the early morning hours to get ahead of the first players.
  Director Wahba stated that he will contact the Country Club to ask about changes to their hours of
  operation.

  COMMISSIONER SCOTT asked about the gates being closed during the day. Director Wahba
  stated there were several meetings with the developer, City Attorney and City Council and ultimately
  the City Council decided not to adopt the gate protocol and are now able to have the gate closed at
  all times.

  COMMISSIONER MEDAWAR left the meeting at 7:50 p.m.

  COMMISSIONER CARMAN asked about the Nature Center and the use of the facility. After
  reviewing the Joint Meeting Park & Activities minutes, she is concerned that they may be getting too
  far into the design without doing the necessary studies. Director Wahba stated that he is working on
  getting a list of the types of uses, hours, and what the occupancy will be. This list is necessary to
  get a proposal for an environmental consultant to do an initial study, which will drive the parking and
  traffic studies that will need to be done. There is also discussion on potential parking on Palos
  Verdes Drive East and restricting parking on Hitching Post Drive. If there is an event where more
  parking is required, they will need to make secure parking at one of the church facilities and have
  shuttle service to the Nature Center. Director Wahba provided an overview on the process and
  stated that the Planning Commission will have an opportunity to review the project and the
  environmental document and add conditions of approval. COMMISSIONER CARMAN expressed
  her concerns with this project.

  10.  PLANNING MANAGER ITEMS

  PLANNING MANAGER NAUGHTON stated that the Housing Elements should be coming to the
  Planning Commission next month.

  11.  MATTERS OF INFORMATION

  A.  CITY COUNCIL ACTIONS - JANUARY 26, 2021

  B.  CITY COUNCIL ACTIONS - FEBRUARY 9, 2021

  C.  PARK AND ACTIVITIES COMMISSION DRAFT MINUTES - JANUARY 27, 2021

  VICE CHAIR made a motion to,

  RECEIVE AND FILE ITEMS 11A – 11C

  There being no objection, CHAIR EDLER so ordered.

  10.  ADJOURNMENT

  CHAIR CARMAN adjourned the meeting at 8:05 pm to the next Special Planning Commission
  meeting on Monday, May 3, 2021 at 7:00 p.m., which will be held by Video Teleconference.

PLANNING COMMISSION MEETING
MINUTES, APRIL 5, 2021
  3
   Respectfully submitted,  Approved,

  Carol Corea, Administrative Assistant  Rick Edler, Chair
